definitions.explanation: A form of Japanese poetry with the same 5-7-5 syllable structure as haiku, but focusing on human nature, satire, or humor rather than nature and seasons.

examples.japanese: {川柳|せんりゅう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
{川柳|せんりゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詠|よ}む→詠む：14186_yomu⟧。
⟦{俳句|はいく}→俳句：00083_haiku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{違|ちが}って→違う：01957_chigau⟧、{川柳|せんりゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{要|い}らない→要る：09589_iru⟧。
examples.english: Unlike haiku, senryu don't require a seasonal word.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
{川柳|せんりゅう} shares the 5-7-5 mora form of ⟦{俳句|はいく}→俳句：00083_haiku⟧ but not its rules:
- no ⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧ (seasonal word) is required;
- the subject is people and daily life, usually with humor, irony, or satire;
- colloquial language is normal.
Newspapers and companies run popular {川柳|せんりゅう} contests (⟦サラリーマン→サラリーマン：06084_sarariiman⟧{川柳|せんりゅう}, about office life).

ETYMOLOGY:
Named after {柄井川柳|からいせんりゅう}, an Edo-period judge of verse contests whose selections made the form popular.
